coverage_explanation: Exercises successful initialization at 9600 baud and fresh acceleration reporting across five controlled sensor states, including signed independent axis changes, zero acceleration, and return to an earlier state. Numeric checks do not prescribe labels or numeric notation. They establish presence of the expected numbers, but cannot independently establish X/Y/Z association, membership in the same sample, or three separate zero-valued axis results. Textual unit annotation, library selection, I2C transactions, and execution of delay(500) in every loop are not independently verified. No serial cadence assertion is imposed: a 500ms loop delay does not specify an upper bound on total loop duration. Reporting windows are practical finite observation opportunities, not an inferred maximum reporting latency. Sensor connection failure cannot be injected by this bench.
assumptions: Preserve the supplied Uno wiring: MPU6050 VCC to 3.3V, SDA to A4, SCL to A5, and sensor ground to the common Arduino ground net. The GND.2 connection and GND.3 description are electrically equivalent ground connections.
Serial baud is explicitly 9600. Report labels and numeric representation are unrestricted because the displayed report format is an example.
Native IMU acceleration stimuli are physical values in m/s²; gyro vectors are in rad/s. No raw integers are substituted into physical gyro vectors.
The host reports successful sensor initialization. No initialization-failure behavior is specified or tested.
No LED, button, analog-input, or other default bench wiring is needed.
The reference chooses two decimal places and includes unit text; these reference formatting choices are not imposed on candidates.
Each input state persists for at least three seconds. Numeric tolerance of 0.03 m/s² allows ordinary two-decimal printing and sensor quantization.
